description: Kilo is a multi-cloud network overlay built on WireGuard and designed for Kubernetes (k8s + wg = kg)

summary.one_liner: Kilo is a multi-cloud network overlay built on WireGuard that connects Kubernetes nodes and clusters into one encrypted layer 3 network.
summary.what_it_does: Kilo runs the `kg` agent on every node, which sets up WireGuard keys and routing rules so the pod network stays fully connected across data centers, public clouds, and NAT'd networks. Nodes are grouped into locations using the topology.kubernetes.io/region label or the kilo.squat.ai/location annotation, and one node per location needs a routable public endpoint. It can run as a standalone network provider or in add-on mode on top of Flannel, keeping Flannel for local networking. The README also describes a VPN feature that lets peers outside the cluster join the WireGuard mesh via a Kilo Peer resource and `wg setconf`, and multi-cluster services that link two clusters using the `kgctl` tool. Installation is by deploying a DaemonSet, with example manifests given for kubeadm, bootkube, Typhoon, and k3s.
use_cases: connect Kubernetes nodes across multiple clouds
build a multi-cloud or multi-data-center cluster network
VPN into a Kubernetes cluster to reach services
share services between two Kubernetes clusters
add WireGuard overlay on top of Flannel
let external machines join a cluster network securely
how_to_run: Ensure the WireGuard kernel module is available on all nodes (in-tree from Linux 5.6, or use a userspace implementation)
Label or annotate nodes with kilo.squat.ai/location where the cluster does not set topology.kubernetes.io/region
Ensure at least one node per location has a routable public IP, or set kilo.squat.ai/force-endpoint
kubectl apply -f <kilo manifest for your distribution> (kubeadm, bootkube, Typhoon, or k3s), per the README
For add-on mode on Flannel, apply the add-on manifests from the manifests directory
notable: Fully connected pod network even when nodes are behind NAT or in different networks
Can run standalone or as an add-on on top of Flannel
Lets external VPN peers join the cluster mesh via WireGuard configs
Supports multi-cluster services spanning separate Kubernetes clusters
Topology is customizable by location labels or annotations
caveats: Requires WireGuard kernel module on nodes (or a userspace implementation) and an open UDP port
At least one node per location needs a publicly routable IP address
README's install commands are shown with placeholder manifest paths, so exact manifest URLs are not visible in the text
